literal: If asked what is called old friendship, it is friendship that does not in any way breach the rights of intimacy.
translation: If one asks what defines long-standing friendship, it is that friendship which never, in any way, destroys the mutual rights and liberties of intimacy.
modern: பழைமை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எதுவென்றால், நண்பர்கள் தங்களுக்குள் இருக்கும் உரிமையை எக்காரணத்தைக் கொண்டும் சிதைக்காத நட்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essence of long-standing friendship (paḻaimai). The key word here is 'kiḻamai', which refers to the natural right, freedom, or ownership that close friends have over each other. True old friendship is characterized by 'kīḻntiṭā', meaning it does not breach or destroy this mutual liberty. Even when a friend takes liberties or acts without formal permission, the other does not take offense, preserving the deep bond of trust.
